name: Punjab National Bank
title: Punjab National Bank - 532461 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: PNB Q4 FY26 net profit rose 14.4% YoY to INR5,225 crore; GNPA fell to 2.95% and FY27 NIM guided at 2.6-2.7%.
summary.overview: Punjab National Bank reported Q4 FY26 net profit of INR5,225 crore (up 14.4% YoY) and operating profit of INR7,500 crore (up 10.7% YoY), with FY26 operating profit growth of 9.2% above its 8-9% guidance. Asset quality improved: GNPA fell to 2.95% from 3.95% and NNPA to 0.29% from 0.40%, with FY26 slippage ratio at 0.60%. Domestic NIM was 2.61% in Q4 and global NIM 2.47%, below earlier guidance of 2.8-2.9%, and management cut FY27 global NIM guidance to 2.6-2.7%. Management said the Q4 employee cost fall reflected a INR2,121 crore positive impact from AS-15 yield hardening, which flatters profit, and it framed the ECL transition from April 2027 as manageable.

financial_highlights.change: +10.7% YoY vs INR6,776 crore; FY26 +9.2% vs 8-9% guidance
stable across all four quarters of FY26

segments.name: Retail (ex-IBPC)
segments.commentary: Retail book excluding IBPC grew 18.2% YoY; total retail outstanding about INR2.80 lakh crore including IBPC of INR34,049 crore, which management plans to cut by a further INR18,000-20,000 crore.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 19.9% YoY and management cited ~20% QoQ growth; Q4 MSME slippage INR1,106 crore vs INR995 crore a year earlier. Standard MSME advance yield is 9%.

segments.name: Agriculture (priority sector)
segments.commentary: Agri priority sector advances grew 16.2% YoY; Q4 agri slippage INR1,069 crore vs INR1,400 crore a year earlier.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate share of loan book is about 46-47%, targeted to fall to 42% short term and 40% long term; corporate standard yield is 7.55%. Sanctioned over INR4 lakh crore of corporate credit lines in FY26, with INR1.18 lakh crore pending disbursement.

guidance_outlook: Global NIM guided at 2.6-2.7% for FY27, versus 2.8-2.9% earlier; management will revisit the guidance in October after Q1 and Q2 review.
NII growth guided at about 7% for FY27 alongside 12-13% credit growth; management called it conservative and said it may revisit in October.
Management expects Q1 and Q2 FY27 NIM to improve QoQ, with cost of deposits falling about 5 bps from the special-scheme repricing and incremental deposit cost falling 2-3 bps a month.

ECL transition from 1 April 2027: management said capital (CRAR 17.74%), the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR are sufficient; final ECL impact to be quantified in about two quarters (by July).
Plans to open 250 branches in FY27 (primarily South and West) after adding 144 in FY26; LCR to be maintained around 125%.
Credit cost guidance for FY27 is below 0.4%, as referenced by an analyst; no change was disputed on the call.
capex_capacity: Added 144 branches in FY26 and plans 250 more in FY27, mainly in Southern and Western regions.
New zonal office in Bengaluru operationalised.

No fresh capital raise planned: FY26 had INR8,000 crore authorisation (INR4,000 crore CET1 and INR4,000 crore AT1) but no issuance; INR5,890 crore of AT1 and Tier 2 bonds mature in the current year and will not be replaced.
Wage revision due 1 November 2027, so no FY27 provision was taken for it.
demand_pricing: Total SMA-0/1/2 book is INR41,534 crore (3.30% of advances): SMA-0 INR24,643 crore, SMA-1 INR13,970 crore, SMA-2 INR2,922 crore; retail 8.21%, agri 3.06%, MSME 6.43%.
Q4 FY26 fresh slippages INR2,674 crore vs INR2,904 crore a year earlier; FY26 slippages INR2,758 crore vs INR3,001 crore in FY25. Recoveries of INR15,501 crore in FY26 (2.4x slippages).
Digital sanctions exceeded INR1 lakh crore on a gross basis; INR20,873 crore disbursed digitally in Q4 to 4.8 lakh customers, about one in three loans.
Deposit rates remained sticky; management said cost of deposits has not fallen as expected despite the repo cut, and the Dec-2025 cut hit fully in Q4 versus 26 days in Q3.
Yield on standard domestic advances is 8.23%, above the 7.55% corporate yield.

qa_highlights.question: Why did employee cost fall sharply QoQ to INR3,747 crore and what is the AS-15 effect?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO Raman Grover said AS-15 provisions of INR1,150 crore, INR700 crore and INR700 crore were booked in Q1-Q3; in Q4 no further provision was needed due to bond yield hardening, so INR736 crore is held as prepaid AS-15 and INR1,814 crore was booked to employee cost. Total positive impact cited as INR2,121 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the tax rate rise to about 26.16%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 tax was booked at the 25.168% rate plus disallowances, giving an effective 26.16%; Q3 had a reversal of about INR506 crore of earlier provisions, which lowered the Q3 rate to 19.44%.

qa_highlights.question: Why was NIM guided down to 2.6-2.7% and can it return to 2.8-2.9%?
qa_highlights.answer: Ashok Chandra said deposit rates stayed elevated and bond yields are high, so management chose a conservative 2.6-2.7% range, to be reviewed in Q3 FY27 after watching Q1 and Q2.

qa_highlights.question: How do 12-13% credit growth and 7% NII growth reconcile with NIM expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said NII guidance is conservative given the uncertain corporate book; RAM share is ~54% and targeted to reach 56-57% this year, with corporate falling toward 40% long term, which should lift yields.

qa_highlights.question: Was the ILFS and Sterling Biotech write-back accounted for, and why did standard asset provisions reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: Sterling Biotech (a technical write-off) was factored into operating profit. ILFS is still held under standard provision and may be released in Q1 or Q2. The INR727 crore standard-asset provision release reflects RBI's modified large borrower framework effective 1 January 2026.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECL transition impact and effect on run-rate credit cost and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final number awaits about two more quarters; the earlier draft estimate was INR9,000-10,000 crore shortfall. Management said the INR2,045 crore floating provision and 97% PCR can absorb it and that ROA will stay above 1%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook on the West Asia conflict's impact on MSME and exporters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has seen no challenge in the book so far and held two webinars with exporters and importers in affected areas.

risks_watch: ECL transition from April 2027: final impact unquantified, with management reviewing in about two quarters (by July) and the INR9,000-10,000 crore draft shortfall figure not confirmed.
NIM and cost of deposits: Q4 NIM 2.61% domestic and 2.47% global; cost of deposits fell only 4 bps in Q4 and management expects only about 5 bps further improvement.
Profit quality: Q4 employee cost was flattered by AS-15 reversals (INR2,121 crore positive per management) and treasury income was subdued.
Corporate concentration (46-47% of book) and West Asia conflict exposure to exporters and importers.
Tax rate rose to 26.16% in Q4 after a Q3 reversal; Q1 FY26 had a one-time hit from the new tax regime.
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality, capital and slippages, but cautious on margins: management deliberately cut NIM guidance to 2.6-2.7% and NII growth to about 7%, and deflected several questions on ECL quantification and profit drivers.
key_quotes: We met or exceeded our stated guidance for 2025-'26 financial year across most key parameters.
So we have kept the slippages fully under control.
So we thought that instead of giving 2.8%, 2.9% and showing a very rosy picture and coming down, we thought let us keep that 2.6% to 2.7%.
And this time, because of the hardening of the government security rates, there was no need of making further provisions in AS -15.
So we have enough cushion to take care of any requirement which will come on account of implementation of ECL from 1st of April 2027.

adds.what: 250 new branches planned in FY27, mainly South and West (after 144 added in FY26)

growth.why: FY27 NII growth guided at about 7% with 12-13% credit growth, and global NIM cut to 2.6-2.7% from 2.8-2.9%; backing is partial (branch rollout and deposit repricing) with no specific capacity or order numbers beyond branch count.
